title: fix(update): avoid duplicate snapshots during candidate readiness
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes redundant database snapshot work while the updater waits for candidate readiness with a cold recovery reader and no startup warning.

## User Impact

Future updater runs perform fewer blocking snapshot children in this readiness path. Four synthetic probes require 8 snapshots instead of 16. This does not patch an already-running or older installed updater, and the measurements are not a whole-upgrade speedup claim.

## Why This Change Was Made

The readiness owner awaited an already-resolved placeholder warning promise twice per probe, then repeated the recovery/authority check. A cold recovery read can launch a synchronous SQLite snapshot child.

Represent absent warning work explicitly and await it only once a real warning exists. Checks still bracket every async probe; warning settlement, cancellation, generation/custody checks, leases, rollback, and exact-version verification retain their existing behavior. No workers, concurrency, caches, schema/config changes, or timeout increases were added. Production delta: +5 lines; tests: +108.

## Evidence

Current head: `83b04f36f85846c2ade424952c98f269ce56752c`. Pinned base: `6693bb9665ced2a4fea3e286f62acfd0116e2c72`.

- [Required CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37477603744) passed on this head; both `openclaw/ci-gate` publishers are successful.
- [Isolated source, package, and installed-update qualification](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37478065600): **PASS** published **2026.9.8** driver × exact **2026.9.8** candidate. Update exited 0 in **277.661s**; cell completed in **354.15s**. Durable status is finished/succeeded, `readyz=200`, installed build metadata and running version verified. Durable chat content survived restart; incognito history and artifacts did not. Container runtime: **Node 24.21.0 / SQLite 3.53.4**. This is a disposable managed-service fixture, not a production upgrade.
- Six focused regressions pass: the two real-database recovery tests and four existing warning-write failure, authority revocation, late-deadline uncertainty, and cancelled-sleep uncertainty cases. New cases took 2.121s and 0.627s. Cold focused wrapper: 40.02s, including 24.21s of worker compilation; warning wrapper: 18.70s. Compact hosted CI logs do not expose per-file seconds.
- Complete 52,797-file source inventory verified around the frozen physical dependency install, after comparison source restoration, and after packaging. Package build/integrity passed in 663.09s; peak build RSS 9,623,536 KiB, no swaps. `git diff --check` passes.
- Comparison below ran baseline/candidate/candidate/baseline on one lease: Node **24.19.0**, SQLite **3.53.3**, pnpm **12.5.1**, Linux x64, eight visible CPUs and 30.95 GiB RAM. Both baseline runs fail the new snapshot budget; both candidate runs pass.

Identical closed SQLite seed in all four trials: **1,482,752 bytes**, SHA-256 `af1623b44575cf5b6e2ae18a8e65edb5cdc72eb89a3b4683e0ccd88f416eef4e`. Four responses: two starting, startup success, readiness success. Real recovery reads and snapshots; HTTP and retry sleep are simulated. Source database bytes remain unchanged.

| Trial | Snapshots | Readiness wall (ms) | Parent CPU user+system (ms) | Parent process peak RSS (KiB) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Baseline 1 | 16 | 3702.81 | 189.87 | 767840 |
| Candidate 2 | 8 | 2236.31 | 179.70 | 786992 |
| Candidate 3 | 8 | 1678.27 | 91.84 | 816824 |
| Baseline 4 | 16 | 3040.73 | 135.17 | 778428 |

Median readiness: **3371.77 → 1957.29ms**, **42.0% lower** across two observations per variant. CPU excludes children; peak RSS includes imports/setup. These samples establish no memory improvement. Snapshot work stays sequential; peak temporary storage was not separately sampled.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction, review notes, and limits</summary>

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/update-cli/update-command-recovery-cost.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/update-candidate-canary.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 --testNamePattern='preserves uncertain startup warning identity|joins a startup warning'
```

Run the new regression with only the readiness implementation replaced by the pinned base to reproduce `expected 16 to be less than or equal to 8`. The timed comparison freezes one generated, closed SQLite seed and measures only `f.readiness()` with `performance.now()`, `process.cpuUsage()`, and `process.resourceUsage().maxRSS`.

Owner chain: candidate validation → readiness → CLI execution guard → retained recovery → artifact-preserving reader → synchronous snapshot child. CPU/I/O activity by itself did not establish deadlock or justify more threads. Real async warning waits remain necessary.

An initial 2026.9.7 candidate was correctly rejected after the 2026.9.8 driver wrote newer config metadata. That concrete failing guard prompted one pinned-base refresh; `git range-diff` confirms an identical patch. No version guard was weakened. A smaller Testbox was stopped at resource preflight before tests/build; qualification then used the native memory-heavy lane.

Validated tarball: **105,328,998 bytes**, SHA-256 `0188242e572c1ce91d49caf333f4e557ed7c56f370469afb8b4d0f52784a4ad8`. Build ID: `2026.9.8-83b04f36f858-2026-10-06T14-25-51.644Z`. Candidate package and config versions were not relabeled.

ClawSweeper reviewed this exact head and found no introduced code defect; its installed-driver qualification request is addressed by the result above. No additional independent execution worker was started, per task scope. No live upgrade, fleet, macOS runtime, or Bun-specific proof was run. Local Node 26.7.0 and Bun 1.3.14 were unchanged and unused for runtime proof. Release-note context stays here because the changelog is release-owned.

The related warning settlement repair in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/161104 remains intact; the progress changes in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/162345 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/162604 do not remove these empty waits.
</details>
